messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager alert — Severity: P1. Observed sustained 5xx increase and token latency > 2s for org=atlasia-inc across us-west-2. Auto-created incident IR-2026-198. Paging oncall: @Jamie Chen.
Jamie Chen: on it. joining call now — hopping into infra dashboard.
Maria Gomez: FYI I can watch QPS & tokens. I'm seeing a spike to ~1800 rps from atlasia and error rate up to 4.8% on route /v1/generate (avg before was 0.2%).
Jamie Chen: thanks. any recent deploys for atlasia models or canary? @Arjun?
Arjun Patel: no full deploys. They did enable new streaming mode yesterday but that shouldn't change request volume. Looks like a customer-side marketing campaign. Sales ping?
Liz Carter: confirmed — atlasia ran an unannounced webinar a few minutes ago and forwarded a link. They're hitting our hosted API hard. I've reached out to their SRE.
Ryan Cho: whole-tenant rate limiter kicking, but their quota was set high (org_quota.qps=2000). The backend queue is backed up; tail latencies at GPU nodes hitting 3.5s.
Jamie Chen: we need a quick mitigation to protect other customers. Options: (A) global throttling (bad), (B) per-org soft cap reduce, (C) temporary bump and schedule dedicated capacity. Prefer (B) — lower atlasia to safer qps until they agree to commit. @Maria what reduction would buy breathing room?
Maria Gomez: lowering to 600 qps will bring error rate down under 0.5% and restore latency. We can roll that instantly.
Arjun Patel: agree. Prepare rollback plan. If they complain, we can offer dedicated capacity/upgrade.
Jamie Chen: @Ashwin can you apply the per-org cap change? Use admin API. I'll coordinate notices.
Ashwin Rao: doing it now.
Ashwin Rao: __executing__:
```
# internal admin API
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/api/v1/orgs/atlasia-inc/adjust" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"action":"set_qps","value":600,"reason":"emergency mitigation - global stability"}'
```
Ashwin Rao: response 200 OK. change_id=chg-2026-IR198-01
Maria Gomez: monitoring… error rate dropping to 0.6% and p95 latency down from 3.5s to 380ms. Good signal.
Jamie Chen: notify atlasia contacts with friendly heads-up and ask them to throttle client-side or request dedicated capacity.
Liz Carter: messaging outbound to atlasia SRE + CSM now: "We're seeing a large traffic surge from your account causing platform impact. We've temporarily set a per-org cap to 600 QPS to protect service for all customers. Please coordinate with us if you need dedicated capacity or a quota increase." Will paste thread here.
Samir Kaur: pinged on email + slack. Their SRE (kevin@atlasia) acknowledged and said they'll throttle some jobs in 7-10 minutes.
Jamie Chen: good. Put a canary to slowly raise if they prove client-side controls. For now keep cap at 600.
Ryan Cho: adding an automated rule to block bursts from new IP pools for this org for next 30m — done.
Maria Gomez: also re-enabled KV prefix caching for atlasia's common prompts; that reduced token compute by ~20%.
Jamie Chen: thanks team. Is there any customer-facing outage noted in support? @Samir or @Liz
Samir Kaur: support log: 3 tickets complaining about slow responses starting at 1864123380. Marked them as "mitigated - temporary cap applied" and linking this thread.
Arjun Patel: postmortem action items: (1) automated detection for org-level burst patterns, (2) self-serve guardrail that suggests Dedicated offer at 75% of org quota, (3) more visible org quota on console.
Jamie Chen: I'll take (1) and (3). @Arjun can you lead (2) with Product? Track in IR-2026-198.
Liz Carter: Atlasia replied — "thanks, we mis-configured a cron that started pushing traffic" and asked for a temporary increase to 1200 while they complete fixes. Not approving yet; need to see telemetry hold low for 20m.
Maria Gomez: we can do a stepped bump after 20m: 600 -> 900 for 10m -> evaluate. If metrics remain healthy, consider 1200.
Jamie Chen: agree. schedule bump in 20m as a canary with rollback on error rate > 1% or p95 > 600ms.
Ashwin Rao: scheduling bump via admin change chg-2026-IR198-02 at 1864124556. (Will execute only if manual go) — leaving the scheduler locked until someone clicks confirm.
Jamie Chen: I'll hold the manual go. For audit: change log chg-2026-IR198-01 created by Ashwin at 1864123501. linked to incident IR-2026-198.
IncidentBot: Incident IR-2026-198 status: mitigation applied (org cap set to 600 qps). Incident owners: Jamie Chen, Maria Gomez. Slack thread linked. Auto-escalation timer set to 30m.
Jamie Chen: closing paging oncall for now. Team continue monitoring and update incident ticket. Thanks all — great fast work. :thumbsup:
Maria Gomez: will post final numbers and RCA once traffic stabilizes. Initial impact: prevented platform-wide latency increase; ~0.01% of customers impacted by the defensive cap window.
Samir Kaur: logging follow-up notes and customer comms in the incident doc.
Arjun Patel: adding a short-runbook entry: "Emergency per-org qps adjust — who can flip admin API + metrics gates." Will link to runbook repo.
Liz Carter: capturing billing/sales follow-up — likely opportunity for Dedicated contract.
Jamie Chen: adding this thread to the incident and will draft a blameless postmortem. If anyone has additional notes, append here."
